sections.title: Everyday In-Progress Expressions
sections.content:
When talking on the phone or texting, native speakers constantly use *estar + gerundio* to give real-time updates:
- **Estoy saliendo**: I am on my way out / leaving
- **Estoy llegando**: I am arriving / almost there
- **¿Me estás escuchando?**: Can you hear me? / Are you listening to me?
- **¿Qué estás haciendo?**: What are you up to right now?

sections.title: Common Phone Expressions
rows: I am arriving at the café.

items.spanish: Hola Carlos, ¿dónde estás? Estoy saliendo del metro.
items.english: Hello Carlos, where are you? I'm coming out of the subway.

items.spanish: Hay mucho ruido, no te estoy escuchando bien.
items.english: There is a lot of noise, I am not hearing you well.

items.spanish: Te mando un mensaje, estoy conduciendo.
items.english: I'll text you, I am driving.

sections.content: Pronoun placement: Reflexive or object pronouns can go either BEFORE *estar* (*Me estoy vistiendo*) or ATTACHED to the gerund (*Estoy vistiéndome*). At A1, placing them before is the simplest and most common strategy.
